title: Keep every judgment whole
statement: Keep every judgment whole, so it can be replayed or re-asked of another judge; where two judges agree against an answer key, check the key.
detail:
Every try's decide records are kept as decide made them, so a block can be re-judged through a second judge
(`g9/transformer/src/blocks.js`); a replayed session must match tick for tick and never ask the judge
(`g9/transformer/src/quality/playtest.js`), and the first replay gave 8 ticks, 0 differences
(`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, "Live session"). Replayed through a second judge, the reading engine's recorded session
agreed on 0.946 of 37 judgments (`grade3-reading/engine/EVIDENCE-2026-09-22.md`); where the judge disagreed with the
authored key, stably across three runs, the key was at fault: it included two fragments that describe nothing and
missed two that do (the same file).
against:
records missing a part are counted, not replayed, and agreement with a
second judge is the cheapest signal, not accuracy (`g9/transformer/src/quality/calibrate.js`).

- golden-001 (math g3 mcq easy): INFERIOR → SUPERIOR (BAML correctly rates it; no failing metrics)

golden-001 (grade 3 MCQ on parallel sides) has a labeled answer of B=1 with the explanation "A triangle has one pair of parallel sides: the bottom side is parallel to itself." A triangle has zero pairs of parallel sides, and no standard geometry treats a side as parallel to itself — the correct answer is A=0.

item's evaluator score sits on the pass/fail boundary and may vary between INFERIOR and ACCEPTABLE/SUPERIOR across runs. It is pinned to ACCEPTABLE to reflect its typical post-fix behaviour while acknowledging inherent instability.
